greetSimpler.en: Today we talk about lines that never meet, and lines that meet at a square corner.

asidePark.hi: {aside} ki baat bhi hogi, bas yeh rekhaon wala kaam khatam ho jaaye.

asidePark.hi: Mazedaar, {aside} ki baat hum zaroor karenge, bas thodi der mein.
asidePark.en: Fun, we will surely talk about {aside}, just in a little while.

backTo.hi: Achha, ab pehle wale sawaal ko phir se dekhte hain.

hook.convey: two straight lines going the same way side by side → the gap between them never changes → they never meet however far they go; rail tracks, the two creases at a cricket pitch end (different lengths, still side by side), ruled lines of a drawing copy

use.hi: Train ki do patriyan hamesha ek hi disha mein chalti hain. Unke beech ki doori har jagah ek jaisi rehti hai, isliye kitni bhi door jaao, patriyan kabhi nahi milti.
use.en: The two rails of a train track always run in the same direction. The gap between them is the same everywhere, so however far you go, the rails never meet.

use.hi: Cricket pitch ke ek sire par bowling crease aur popping crease ek hi disha mein kheenchi jaati hain, aur unke beech har jagah barabar doori hoti hai. Popping crease zyada lambi hoti hai, phir bhi dono saath-saath chalti hain.
use.en: At one end of a cricket pitch the bowling crease and the popping crease are drawn in the same direction, with the same gap between them everywhere. The popping crease is longer, yet the two still run side by side.

use.hi: Drawing copy ki lines dekho: har line agli line se barabar doori par hai, page ke baayein kinaare se daayein kinaare tak.
use.en: Look at the lines of a drawing copy: each line is the same distance from the next, from the left edge of the page to the right edge.

explain.convey: parallel = same direction + gap the same everywhere → never meet, however far extended; AB above CD, gap 3 cm at the left edge and 3 cm at the right edge; the child then adds a third parallel line EF 2 cm below CD → AB to EF = 3 + 2 = 5 cm

mustSay.en: the gap is the same everywhere

point.hi: Page par do seedhi lines hain, upar AB aur neeche CD. Baayein kinaare par AB se CD tak doori 3 cm hai, aur daayein kinaare par bhi 3 cm. Doori har jagah barabar hai, toh dono ek hi disha mein chalti hain, aur page kitna bhi lamba karo, kabhi nahi milengi. Aisi lines ko parallel lines kehte hain.
point.en: There are two straight lines on the page, AB on top and CD below. At the left edge the gap from AB to CD is 3 cm, and at the right edge it is also 3 cm. The gap is the same everywhere, so both run in the same direction, and however long you make the page, they will never meet. Such lines are called parallel lines.

prompt.hi: AB aur CD ke beech doori 3 cm hai. CD ke neeche ek teesri line EF kheenchi, jo CD ke parallel hai aur CD se 2 cm door hai. AB aur EF ke beech doori kitni hai?
prompt.en: The gap between AB and CD is 3 cm. Below CD a third line EF is drawn, parallel to CD and 2 cm away from it. What is the gap between AB and EF?

why.hi: AB se CD 3 cm hai aur CD se EF 2 cm, aur 3 + 2 = 5
why.en: AB to CD is 3 cm and CD to EF is 2 cm, and 3 + 2 = 5

simpler.hi: Parallel lines ke beech doori har jagah ek jaisi rehti hai, jaise yahan dono kinaaron par 3 cm. Isliye woh kabhi nahi milti.
simpler.en: The gap between parallel lines stays the same everywhere, like 3 cm at both edges here. That is why they never meet.

explain.convey: length plays no part: segment PQ 2 cm, RS 7 cm, same direction, gap from PQ's two ends to RS 4 cm both times → the child decides parallel from direction and gap, not from length

point.hi: Segment PQ sirf 2 cm lamba hai, aur segment RS ki lambai 7 cm hai. Dono ek hi disha mein jaate hain. PQ ke dono siron se RS tak doori naapi, aur dono jagah 4 cm aayi. Ab socho, PQ ko usi disha mein aage badhao toh kya hota hai.
point.en: Segment PQ is only 2 cm long and segment RS is 7 cm. Both go in the same direction. The gap from each end of PQ to RS was measured, and it came out 4 cm both times. Now think about what happens if PQ is extended in the same direction.

prompt.hi: PQ 2 cm lamba hai aur RS ki lambai 7 cm; disha ek hai aur doori dono jagah 4 cm hai. Kya PQ aur RS parallel hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: PQ is 2 cm long and RS is 7 cm; the direction is the same and the gap is 4 cm at both places. Are PQ and RS parallel, yes or no?

why.hi: segment PQ ki lambai 2 cm aur RS ki 7 cm, par disha ek hai aur doori dono jagah 4 cm
why.en: PQ is 2 cm and RS is 7 cm, but they share one direction and a 4 cm gap

simpler.hi: Chhote segment ko bhi aage badhaya ja sakta hai. Parallel ke liye lambai nahi, sirf disha aur doori dekhte hain.
simpler.en: Even a short segment can be extended. For parallel, we look only at direction and gap, not length.

explain.convey: not meeting on the page is not enough: gap 6 cm at the left edge, 4 cm at the right edge of a 20 cm page → the gap shrinks 1 cm every 10 cm → it reaches 0 off the page, so the lines meet; the child works out where

point.hi: Yeh do seedhi lines bhi page par kahin nahi milti. Par baayein kinaare par unke beech doori 6 cm hai aur daayein kinaare par sirf 4 cm. Doori ghat rahi hai, matlab lines dheere-dheere ek-doosre ki taraf aa rahi hain, aur page ke bahar bhi aati rahengi.
point.en: These two straight lines also never meet on the page. But at the left edge the gap between them is 6 cm, and at the right edge only 4 cm. The gap is shrinking, which means the lines are slowly coming towards each other, and they keep coming beyond the page too.

prompt.hi: Page 20 cm chauda hai, toh baayein se daayein jaate hue doori har 10 cm par 1 cm ghatti hai. Daayein kinaare ke aage kitne centimetre jaakar yeh lines milengi?
prompt.en: The page is 20 cm wide, so going from left to right the gap shrinks by 1 cm every 10 cm. How many centimetres beyond the right edge will these lines meet?

why.hi: daayein kinaare par doori 4 cm hai, aur har 10 cm mein 1 cm ghatti hai: 4 × 10 = 40
why.en: the gap at the right edge is 4 cm, and it shrinks 1 cm every 10 cm: 4 × 10 = 40

simpler.hi: Yahan doori 6 cm se ghat kar 4 cm ho gayi. Ghatti doori matlab lines paas aa rahi hain, aage jaakar zaroor milengi.
simpler.en: Here the gap shrinks from 6 cm to 4 cm. A shrinking gap means the lines are coming closer, and further on they will surely meet.

problem.hi: Ek deewar par do seedhi shelves lagi hain, upar wali 90 cm lambi aur neeche wali 60 cm. Inke beech doori naapi gayi: baayein taraf 25 cm, beech mein 25 cm, aur daayein taraf bhi 25 cm. Kya dono shelves parallel hain?
problem.en: Two straight shelves are fixed on a wall, the upper one 90 cm long and the lower one 60 cm. The gap between them was measured: 25 cm on the left, 25 cm in the middle and 25 cm on the right as well. Are the two shelves parallel?

simpler.hi: Shelves ki lambai chhodo. Sirf unke beech ki doori dekho, ki teeno jagah wahi hai ya alag.
simpler.en: Forget the shelves' lengths. Look only at the gap between them, whether it is the same at all three places or not.

givens.hi: upar wali shelf 90 cm aur neeche wali 60 cm lambi hai
givens.en: the upper shelf is 90 cm long and the lower one 60 cm

givens.hi: doori baayein taraf, beech mein aur daayein taraf, teeno taraf 25 cm hai
givens.en: the gap is 25 cm on the left, in the middle and on the right

find.hi: dono shelves parallel hain ya nahi
find.en: whether the two shelves are parallel

do.hi: Teeno taraf ki doori aapas mein milao

steps.result: teeno taraf doori 25 cm, koi badlaav nahi

why.hi: doori na ghati na badhi, toh shelves na paas aa rahi hain na door ja rahi hain
why.en: the gap neither shrank nor grew, so the shelves are neither coming closer nor moving apart

simpler.hi: Teeno jagah doori 25 cm naapi gayi. Teeno number ek jaise hain, toh doori kahin nahi badli.
simpler.en: The gap was 25 cm at all three places. All three numbers match, so the gap did not change anywhere.

do.hi: Ab dono shelves ki lambai dekho
do.en: Now look at the lengths of the two shelves

steps.result: upar wali 90 cm, neeche wali 60 cm, lambai alag

why.hi: 60 cm wali shelf ko usi disha mein aage badhao toh woh 90 cm wali ke saath-saath hi chalegi
why.en: if the 60 cm shelf is extended in the same direction, it just runs alongside the 90 cm one

simpler.hi: Ek shelf 90 cm ki hai, doosri 60 cm ki. Lambai alag hai, bas itna dhyan mein rakho.
simpler.en: One shelf is 90 cm, the other 60 cm. The lengths are different; just keep that in mind.

prompt.hi: Doori teeno jagah 25 cm hai, par ek shelf 90 cm aur doosri 60 cm lambi hai. Kya parallel hone ke liye dono shelves ki lambai barabar honi zaroori hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: The gap is 25 cm at all three places, but one shelf is 90 cm and the other 60 cm long. To be parallel, must the two shelves be the same length, yes or no?

simpler.hi: Parallel ke liye lambai nahi, sirf doori dekhte hain. Yahan doori har jagah 25 cm hi hai.
simpler.en: For parallel we look at the gap, not the length. Here the gap is 25 cm everywhere.

why.hi: upar wali shelf 90 cm aur neeche wali 60 cm, par doori har jagah 25 cm, toh lambai se kuch nahi badalta
why.en: the upper shelf is 90 cm and the lower 60 cm, but the gap is 25 cm everywhere: length changes nothing

answer.hi: haan, dono shelves parallel hain; lambai alag hone se kuch nahi badalta
answer.en: yes, the two shelves are parallel; the different lengths change nothing

why.hi: dono ek hi disha mein hain aur doori har jagah 25 cm hai; shelf ki lambai se koi farak nahi padta
why.en: both go in the same direction and the gap is 25 cm everywhere; a shelf's length does not affect being parallel

prompt.hi: EF 4 cm lamba hai. GH, EF ke parallel hai aur har jagah usse 3 cm door. GH kitna lamba ho sakta hai: sirf 4 cm, ya koi bhi lambai?
prompt.en: EF is 4 cm long. GH is parallel to EF and 3 cm from it everywhere. How long can GH be: only 4 cm, or any length?

accept: koi bhi lambai ho sakti hai

why.hi: GH har jagah 3 cm door hai; parallel disha aur doori se tay hota hai, toh GH kitna bhi lamba ho
why.en: GH is 3 cm away everywhere; parallel depends on direction and gap, so GH can be any length

simpler.hi: Lambai se parallel tay nahi hota. Socho ki GH ko usi disha mein badhaane par doori badalti hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: Length does not decide parallel. Think whether extending GH in the same direction changes the gap or not.

prompt.hi: Do seedhi lines page par kahin nahi milti. Baayein kinaare par unki doori 7 cm hai aur page ke theek beech mein 6 cm. Daayein kinaare par doori kitni hogi?
prompt.en: Two straight lines do not meet anywhere on the page. Their gap is 7 cm at the left edge and 6 cm at the exact middle of the page. What will the gap be at the right edge?

why.hi: baayein kinaare se beech tak doori 7 se 6 cm hui; baaki aadhe mein bhi 1 cm ghategi, toh 5 cm
why.en: from the left edge to the middle the gap fell from 7 to 6 cm; it falls 1 cm more: 5 cm

simpler.hi: Seedhi lines ki doori ek jaisi raftaar se ghatti hai. Aadhe page mein jitni ghati, baaki aadhe mein bhi utni hi ghategi.
simpler.en: The gap between straight lines shrinks at a steady rate. As much as it shrank over half the page, it shrinks again over the other half.

ladder.why: first look around the room: edges that run side by side with a steady gap
say why a 2 cm and a 10 cm segment can still be parallel: direction, not length
predict: gap 4 cm then 3 cm across the page → they meet off the page, not parallel
contrast ruled lines (steady gap) with lines 2 cm then 1 cm apart; neither touches on the page
real court boundaries 5 m and 4.8 m apart: a small change in the gap still means not parallel

remediation.move: extend the short segment along its own direction: it grows as long as the other while the gap stays put → length can always be changed, so it cannot decide parallel; only direction and gap do

say.hi: Chhote segment ko usi disha mein aage badhao, woh lamba hota jaata hai par doori wahi rehti hai. Lambai toh hum kabhi bhi badha sakte hain, isliye parallel hona sirf disha aur doori se tay hota hai.
say.en: Extend the short segment in the same direction: it keeps getting longer but the gap stays the same. We can always change a length, so being parallel is decided only by direction and gap.

simpler.hi: Segment ko usi disha mein badhao, doori wahi rehti hai. Parallel hona sirf disha aur doori se tay hota hai, lambai se nahi.
simpler.en: Extend the segment in the same direction and the gap stays the same. Being parallel depends only on direction and gap, not length.

prompt.hi: Board ke dono pair dekho: A ki dono lines barabar lambi hain, B ki nahi. Kaunsa pair parallel hai, A ya B?
prompt.en: Look at the two pairs on the board: A's lines are the same length, B's are not. Which pair is parallel, A or B?

why.hi: B ki doori har jagah 2 cm, toh B parallel; A barabar lambi, par doori 3 cm aur 4 cm
why.en: B's gap stays 2 cm, so B is parallel; A's lines are equally long, but the gap is 3 and 4 cm

simpler.hi: Lambai chhodo, sirf dekho kis pair ki doori har jagah ek si hai.
simpler.en: Forget the lengths; just see which pair has the same gap everywhere.

remediation.move: the page edge is not the end of a line: zoom out past the edge; a shrinking gap keeps shrinking until it is 0, and there the lines meet → measure the gap at two places, don't just look for a touch

say.hi: Page ka kinaara line ka ant nahi hai, line aage bhi chalti hai. Agar doori ghat rahi hai, toh aage chalte-chalte woh ghatti hi rahegi, jab tak 0 na ho jaaye.
say.en: The edge of the page is not the end of a line; the line goes on. If the gap is shrinking, it keeps shrinking further along, until it reaches 0.

simpler.hi: Line page ke kinaare par khatam nahi hoti. Ghatti doori aage bhi ghatti rehti hai, 0 tak.
simpler.en: A line does not end at the page edge. A shrinking gap keeps shrinking on, down to 0.

prompt.hi: Lines page par nahi milti. Parallel hain, yeh kaise pakka karoge: sirf dekhkar, ya do door-door jagah doori naapkar?
prompt.en: Lines don't meet on the page. To be sure they're parallel, will you just look, or measure the gap at two far places?

why.hi: page par lines nahi milti, par sirf dekhkar pakka nahi; line aage chalti hai, toh do door jagah doori naapkar dekho
why.en: just looking that they don't meet proves nothing; lines go on past the page, so measure the gap at two far places

simpler.hi: Line page ke bahar bhi chalti hai. Socho, page par na milna kaafi saboot hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: The line goes on beyond the page. Think whether not meeting on the page is proof enough.

bridgeToNext.hi: Parallel lines kabhi nahi milti. Ab hum woh lines dekhenge jo milti hain, aur ek khaas tarah se milti hain, theek samkon par, 90° par.
bridgeToNext.en: Parallel lines never meet. Now we will look at lines that do meet, and meet in a special way, exactly at a right angle, at 90°.

simpler.hi: Ab woh lines dekhenge jo milti hain. Board par do lines ek bindu par mil rahi hain.
simpler.en: Now we look at lines that do meet. On the board two lines meet at one point.

hook.convey: lines that meet at exactly 90° are everywhere, and turning the picture never changes the angle; a road crossing a railway track square-on, the corner of a drawing sheet turned any way

use.hi: Railway crossing par sadak aksar train ki patri ko theek 90° par paar karti hai, taaki car aur bus seedhe nikal sakein.
use.en: At a railway crossing the road often crosses the train track at exactly 90°, so that cars and buses can go straight across.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ko kisi bhi taraf ghuma do, uske har kone par do kinaare 90° par hi milte hain. Sheet tirchhi ho jaaye toh bhi kone ka angle wahi rehta hai.
use.en: Turn a drawing sheet any way you like: at each corner two edges still meet at 90°. Even when the sheet is tilted, the corner's angle stays the same.

explain.convey: perpendicular = two lines meeting at 90° (samkon); the small square mark shows it; board: the two lines crossing with one corner marked 90° → the child works out how many of the four angles at the crossing are 90° (linear pairs: 180 − 90 = 90 each)

point.hi: Yeh do lines ek bindu par ek-doosre ko kaat-ti hain, aur ek kone par unke beech ka angle 90° hai, yaani samkon. Kone par yeh chhota nishaan samkon dikhata hai. Jo do lines 90° par milti hain, unhe perpendicular lines kehte hain.
point.en: These two lines cross each other at a point, and at one corner the angle between them is 90°, that is, a right angle. The small mark at the corner shows the right angle. Two lines that meet at 90° are called perpendicular lines.

prompt.hi: Is crossing par 90° wale kone ke bagal wala angle aur uske saamne wala angle milakar kitne degree ke hain?
prompt.en: At this crossing, how many degrees do the angle next to the 90° corner and the angle opposite that one make together?

why.hi: bagal wala angle 180° − 90° = 90° hai, aur uske saamne wala bhi 90°, toh milakar 90° + 90° = 180°
why.en: the neighbour is 180° − 90° = 90°, the one opposite it is 90° too: together 180°

simpler.hi: Jab do lines milkar kona bilkul 90° ka banati hain, tab woh perpendicular kehlati hain. Kone par bana chhota nishaan isi samkon ko dikhata hai.
simpler.en: When two lines meet and make a corner of exactly 90°, they are called perpendicular. The small mark at the corner shows this right angle.

explain.convey: tilt does not matter: an upright square and the same square turned → every corner still a right angle; pick one side of the tilted square → the child finds how many other sides are perpendicular to it (the 2 neighbours; the opposite side is parallel)

point.hi: Board par do square hain. Pehla seedha rakha hai, aur doosre ko ghuma kar tircha kar diya hai. Ghumaane se kone ka angle nahi badalta, har kone par angle samkon hi rehta hai, chahe koi bhuja seedhi khadi na ho.
point.en: There are two squares on the board. The first stands straight, and the second has been turned so it is tilted. Turning does not change the corner's angle; every corner stays a right angle, even though no side stands straight up.

prompt.hi: Tirche square ki koi ek bhuja chuno. Baaki bhujaon mein se kitni bhujayein us bhuja ke perpendicular hain?
prompt.en: Pick any one side of the tilted square. How many of the other sides are perpendicular to that side?

why.hi: square ke har kone par samkon hai, toh chuni bhuja se judi 2 bhujayein perpendicular hain
why.en: every corner of a square is a right angle, so the 2 sides joined to the chosen side are perpendicular

simpler.hi: Square ko ghumao toh bhi uske kone samkon hi rehte hain. Tircha dikhne se angle nahi badalta.
simpler.en: Even when you turn a square, its corners stay right angles. Looking tilted does not change the angle.

explain.convey: nearly 90° is not 90°: lines meeting at 88° look square but are not perpendicular → the child finds how much more the angle must open (2°)

point.hi: Yeh do lines 86° par milti hain. Dekhne mein lagbhag samkon lagta hai, par perpendicular ke liye angle theek 90° hona chahiye, lagbhag se kaam nahi chalta.
point.en: These two lines meet at 86°. It looks almost like a right angle, but for perpendicular lines the angle must be exactly 90°; almost is not enough.

prompt.hi: Ek line ko ghuma kar angle thoda aur kholna hai, taaki yeh lines perpendicular ban jaayein. Angle ko kitne degree aur kholna hoga?
prompt.en: One line is to be turned to open the angle a little more, so that these lines become perpendicular. By how many more degrees must the angle open?

why.hi: perpendicular ke liye 90° chahiye, aur 90° − 86° = 4°
why.en: perpendicular needs 90°, and 90° − 86° = 4°

simpler.hi: 86° bas paas hai, theek 90° nahi. Perpendicular ke liye angle poora 90° hona chahiye.
simpler.en: 86° is only close, not exactly 90°. Perpendicular needs the full 90°.

problem.hi: Ek ghadi deewar par thodi tirchhi tangi hai. Ghadi par 12 barabar nishaan hain, aur 3:00 baje aur 4:00 baje minute ki sooi 12 par hoti hai. In dono samay par ghante aur minute ki sooiyan perpendicular hain ya nahi?
problem.en: A clock hangs slightly tilted on a wall. The clock has 12 equal marks, and at 3:00 and at 4:00 the minute hand is on 12. At each of these times, are the hour hand and the minute hand perpendicular or not?

simpler.hi: Tirchhi tangi ghadi ke dial par 12 nishaan ek jaisi doori par hain. 3:00 aur 4:00, dono baar minute ki sooi 12 par hai. Dekhna hai ki in samay par sooiyan perpendicular hain ya nahi.
simpler.en: On the tilted clock's dial, 12 marks sit at the same spacing. At 3:00 and at 4:00 the minute hand is on 12. We must see whether the hands are perpendicular at these times.

givens.hi: samay 3:00 aur 4:00 hai, minute ki sooi dono baar 12 par
givens.en: the times are 3:00 and 4:00, with the minute hand on 12 both times

find.hi: 3:00 aur 4:00 par sooiyan perpendicular hain ya nahi
find.en: whether the hands are perpendicular at 3:00 and at 4:00

do.hi: Poore chakkar ko 12 barabar hisson mein baanto
do.en: Divide the full turn into 12 equal parts

steps.result: 360° ÷ 12 = 30°, do paas wale nishaanon ke beech

why.hi: ghadi par 12 barabar nishaan hain aur poora chakkar 360° ka hota hai
why.en: the clock has 12 equal marks and a full turn is 360°

simpler.hi: Poora chakkar 360° ka hota hai, aur ghadi par 12 barabar nishaan hain. 360 ko 12 se baanto, ek hissa mil jaayega.
simpler.en: A full turn is 360°, and the clock has 12 equal marks. Divide 360 by 12 to get one part.

do.hi: 3:00 par sooiyan 12 aur 3 par hain, unke beech 3 hisse hain
do.en: At 3:00 the hands are on 12 and 3, with 3 parts between them

why.hi: angle theek 90° hai, aur ghadi tirchhi ho toh bhi sooiyon ke beech ka angle nahi badalta
why.en: the angle is exactly 90°, and tilting the clock does not change the angle between the hands

simpler.hi: 3:00 par ek sooi 12 par, doosri 3 par hai. Beech mein 3 hisse hain aur har hissa 30° ka, toh 3 baar 30° jodo.
simpler.en: At 3:00 one hand is on 12 and the other on 3. There are 3 parts between them, each 30°, so add 30° three times.

prompt.hi: 4:00 par sooiyan 12 aur 4 par hain. Har hissa 30° ka hai. Sooiyon ke beech angle kitna hai?
prompt.en: At 4:00 the hands are on 12 and 4. Each part is 30°. What is the angle between the hands?

simpler.hi: 4:00 par sooiyon ke beech 4 hisse hain. Har hissa 30° ka hai, toh 4 baar 30° karo.
simpler.en: At 4:00 there are 4 parts between the hands. Each part is 30°, so take 30° four times.

why.hi: 3 baje 90° tha; 4:00 par sooiyan 4 hisse door hain, toh 4 × 30° = 120°
why.en: at 3 o'clock it was 90°; at 4:00 the hands are 4 parts apart, so 4 × 30° = 120°

answer.hi: 3:00 par angle 90° hai, isliye sooiyan perpendicular hain, aur 4:00 par angle 120° hai, isliye nahi
answer.en: at 3:00 the angle is 90°, so the hands are perpendicular, and at 4:00 the angle is 120°, so they are not

why.hi: perpendicular ke liye milne ka angle theek 90° chahiye, sooiyan kis taraf jhuki hain isse koi farak nahi padta
why.en: perpendicular needs the meeting angle to be exactly 90°; which way the hands lean makes no difference

prompt.hi: Ek 3 cm lamba segment aur ek 8 cm lamba segment ek bindu par 90° ka angle banate hain. Kya yeh dono perpendicular hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A 3 cm segment and an 8 cm segment meet at a point at an angle of 90°. Are they perpendicular, yes or no?

why.hi: milne ka angle 90° hai, aur segments ki lambai se farak nahi padta
why.en: the meeting angle is 90°, and the segments' lengths make no difference

simpler.hi: Lambai se farak nahi padta, perpendicular ke liye sirf milne ka angle dekho. Angle 90° hai ya nahi, yahi jaancho.
simpler.en: Length does not matter; for perpendicular look only at the angle where they meet. Check whether that angle is 90°.

prompt.hi: Plus ke nishaan ki dono lines perpendicular hain. Is nishaan ko ghuma kar X jaisa tircha kar diya. Kya X ki dono lines ab bhi perpendicular hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: The two lines of a plus sign are perpendicular. The sign is turned so it is tilted like an X. Are the two lines of the X still perpendicular, yes or no?

why.hi: plus ko ghumaane se X banta hai, par lines ke beech ka angle 90° hi rehta hai
why.en: turning the plus makes an X, but the angle between the lines stays 90°

simpler.hi: Ghumaane se lines ke beech ka angle nahi badalta. Plus ke nishaan mein angle kaisa tha, woh yaad karo.
simpler.en: Turning does not change the angle between the lines. Remember what the angle was in the plus sign.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle frame deewar par tirchha latak gaya. Uske chaar kono mein se kitne kono par bhujayein perpendicular milti hain?
prompt.en: A rectangular frame has slipped and hangs tilted on the wall. At how many of its four corners do the sides meet perpendicularly?

why.hi: frame rectangle hai, har kone par samkon, aur tirchha latakne se kone ka angle nahi badalta: 4 kono par
why.en: the frame is a rectangle, a right angle at every corner, and hanging tilted changes no corner's angle: all 4 corners

simpler.hi: Frame ghoom gaya, par uske kone wahi hain. Socho, rectangle ke kone ka angle kitna hota hai.
simpler.en: The frame has turned, but its corners are the same. Think what angle a rectangle's corner has.

ladder.why: the defining angle: perpendicular lines make 90°
from memory: all four angles at a perpendicular crossing are 90°
paper folding: the second fold onto the first crease makes perpendicular creases
error-spot: tilted lines at 90° called not perpendicular → the angle decides, not the tilt
railway tracks at 88°: nearly square is not perpendicular

remediation.move: set-square rotated onto a tilted crossing: its corner is a fixed right angle whichever way it points → turn the set-square until one edge lies on one line; if the other line lies on the other edge, the lines are perpendicular

say.hi: Set-square ka kona samkon hai. Use kitna bhi ghumao, kone ka angle wahi rehta hai. Isliye tirchhi crossing par set-square ko bhi ghuma kar rakho, kona fit ho jaaye toh lines perpendicular hain.
say.en: The corner of a set-square is a right angle. However much you turn it, the corner's angle stays the same. So on a tilted crossing, turn the set-square too; if the corner fits, the lines are perpendicular.

simpler.hi: Set-square ka kona ghumane par bhi samkon rehta hai. Tirchhi crossing par use ghuma kar rakho; kona fit ho toh lines perpendicular hain.
simpler.en: A set-square's corner stays a right angle when turned. On a tilted crossing, turn it too; if the corner fits, the lines are perpendicular.

prompt.hi: Crossing A: ek line khadi, ek leti, angle 85°. Crossing B: dono lines tirchhi, angle 90°. Perpendicular kaunsi, A ya B?
prompt.en: Crossing A: one line upright, one flat, 85°. Crossing B: both tilted, 90°. Which is perpendicular, A or B?

why.hi: crossing B ka angle theek 90° hai, chahe dono tirchhi hon, aur khadi aur leti A ka 85°
why.en: crossing B's angle is exactly 90° though both are tilted, and A's upright and flat lines make 85°

simpler.hi: Khadi ya leti line dekhne se kuch tay nahi hota. Sirf angle dekho, perpendicular ke liye angle theek 90° chahiye.
simpler.en: Whether a line stands or lies flat decides nothing. Look only at the angle; perpendicular needs exactly 90°.

remediation.move: stretch or shrink one line while the meeting angle stays fixed → length changes, the angle does not → perpendicular is read from the angle alone

say.hi: Perpendicular hone ke liye sirf milne ka angle dekho. Kisi line ko lamba ya chhota karo, milne ka angle wahi rehta hai, aur woh 90° ho toh bas.
say.en: For perpendicular, look only at the angle where the lines meet. Make a line longer or shorter and the meeting angle stays the same; if it is 90°, that is all it takes.

simpler.hi: Sirf milne ka angle dekho. Line lambi ya chhoti karne se woh nahi badalta; 90° ho toh lines perpendicular hain.
simpler.en: Look only at the meeting angle. Making a line longer or shorter does not change it; if it is 90°, the lines are perpendicular.

prompt.hi: 2 cm aur 9 cm ke segment 90° par milte hain. Perpendicular ke liye kya chhote ko 9 cm karna padega?
prompt.en: A 2 cm and a 9 cm segment meet at 90°. To be perpendicular, must the short one become 9 cm?

why.hi: 2 cm aur 9 cm ke segment ka milne ka angle pehle se 90° hai, toh woh perpendicular hain; lambai nahi badalni
why.en: the 2 cm and 9 cm segments already meet at 90°, so they are perpendicular; no length needs to change

simpler.hi: Segment ki lambai se farak nahi padta. Bas dekho ki milne ka angle 90° hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: A segment's length makes no difference. Just see whether the meeting angle is 90°.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab humne parallel aur perpendicular lines pehchaanna seekh liya. Agle hisse mein inhe set-square aur kaagaz ke mod se khud banayenge, aur jaanchenge bhi.
bridgeToNext.en: Now we can recognise parallel and perpendicular lines. In the next part we will draw them ourselves with a set-square and paper folds, and check them too.

simpler.hi: Ab parallel aur perpendicular lines khud banayenge. Board par kaagaz ko modne se ek seedhi crease bani hai.
simpler.en: Now we draw parallel and perpendicular lines ourselves. On the board folding a paper has made a straight crease.

hook.convey: making the lines, not just spotting them: a window grill in a drawing needs parallel bars (set-square slid along a ruler), and zebra-crossing stripes are checked by measuring the gap at both ends

use.hi: Drawing mein khidki ki grill banani ho toh saari khadi pattiyan parallel chahiye. Ruler aur set-square se yeh kaam aasaan ho jaata hai.
use.en: To draw a window grill, all the upright bars need to be parallel. A ruler and a set-square make that easy.

use.hi: Sadak par zebra crossing ki safed pattiyan parallel hoti hain. Painter har patti ke dono siron par doori naap kar jaanchta hai, taaki car aur bus waalon ko seedhi pattiyan dikhein.
use.en: The white stripes of a zebra crossing on a road are parallel. The painter measures the gap at both ends of each stripe, so that car and bus drivers see straight stripes.

explain.convey: paper folding makes a right angle: fold once → a straight crease (a straight angle, 180°); fold again so the crease lies on itself → the 180° is shared into two equal halves → the child works out each angle at the crossing (90°)

point.hi: Kaagaz ko ek baar modo, toh ek seedhi crease banti hai. Ab is crease ko usi ke upar rakh kar kaagaz ko dobara modo, taaki crease ke dono hisse ek-doosre par barabar baithein. Kholo toh do creases ek bindu par milti hain, aur unke beech ke chaaron kone barabar hote hain, har ek samkon.
point.en: Fold a paper once and a straight crease forms. Now fold the paper again so that the crease lies on top of itself, with its two halves sitting exactly on each other. Open it and two creases meet at a point, and the four corners between them are equal, each a right angle.

prompt.hi: Agar doosri baar modte waqt pehli crease khud par theek na baithe, thodi khisak jaaye, toh kya creases ke beech samkon banega, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: If on the second fold the first crease does not lie exactly on itself but slips a little, will the creases make a right angle, yes or no?

why.hi: crease khud par na baithe toh 180° do barabar hisson mein nahi bantta, isliye angle 90° nahi banta
why.en: if the crease does not lie on itself, 180° is not halved, so the angle is not 90°

simpler.hi: Kaagaz do baar modo, crease khud par theek baithe, toh khulne par creases ke beech samkon milta hai.
simpler.en: Fold the paper twice with the crease lying exactly on itself, and when you open it the creases make a right angle.

explain.convey: checking a crossing with a set-square: corner on the meeting point, one edge along one line → the other line along the other edge = right angle; if the other line opens past the edge, the angle is bigger than 90° → the child adds the extra

point.hi: Board par do lines ek crossing banati hain. Set-square ke ek kone par uski do bhujayein samkon banati hain. Jaanchne ke liye yeh kona crossing bindu par rakho aur ek bhuja ko ek line par bithao. Doosri line doosri bhuja ke saath-saath chale toh angle samkon hai, warna nahi.
point.en: On the board two lines make a crossing. At one corner of a set-square its two edges make a right angle. To check, put this corner on the crossing point and lay one edge along one line. If the other line runs along the other edge, the angle is a right angle; if not, it isn't.

prompt.hi: Set-square ka kona ek crossing par rakha. Ek line ek bhuja par theek baithi, par doosri line doosri bhuja se 5° aur bahar khuli hai. Crossing ka angle kitna hai?
prompt.en: A set-square's corner is put on a crossing. One line sits exactly on one edge, but the other line opens 5° further out than the other edge. What is the angle at the crossing?

why.hi: set-square ka kona 90° hai aur line 5° aur bahar khuli hai, 90° + 5° = 95°
why.en: the set-square corner is 90° and the line opens 5° further out, 90° + 5° = 95°

simpler.hi: Set-square ka kona samkon hota hai. Kona crossing par rakho, ek line ek bhuja par, aur dekho doosri line doosri bhuja par baithti hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: A set-square's corner is a right angle. Put the corner on the crossing, one line along one edge, and see if the other line sits along the other edge.

explain.convey: drawing parallels: one set-square edge on the line, ruler held against another edge, slide the set-square along the ruler → it does not turn, so the drawing edge keeps its direction → every line drawn is parallel to the first; lines drawn 2 cm apart each time → the child finds the first-to-third gap

point.hi: Set-square ki ek bhuja ko ruler se sata kar rakho, aur ruler ko kas kar pakdo. Ab set-square ko ruler ke saath khiskao. Woh ghumta nahi, isliye uski doosri bhuja ki disha bhi nahi badalti, aur har jagah kheenchi line pichhli line ke parallel hoti hai.
point.en: Put one edge of the set-square against a ruler and hold the ruler firmly. Now slide the set-square along the ruler. It does not turn, so the direction of its other edge does not change either, and every line drawn is parallel to the one before.

prompt.hi: Isi tarah set-square khiska kar teen parallel lines kheenchi, har agli line pichhli se 2 cm neeche. Pehli aur teesri line ke beech doori kitni hai?
prompt.en: Sliding the set-square this way, three parallel lines are drawn, each one 2 cm below the one before. What is the gap between the first and the third line?

why.hi: pehli se doosri 2 cm aur doosri se teesri 2 cm, aur 2 + 2 = 4
why.en: first to second is 2 cm and second to third is 2 cm, and 2 + 2 = 4

simpler.hi: Set-square ko ruler ke saath sirf khiskao, ghumao mat. Disha same rehti hai, toh har nayi line pichhli line ke parallel banti hai.
simpler.en: Only slide the set-square along the ruler; do not turn it. The direction stays the same, so each new line is parallel to the last.

problem.hi: Page par ek line l kheenchi hai, aur l se 6 cm upar ek bindu P hai. Ruler aur set-square se P se hokar l ke parallel ek line m kheencho, aur jaancho ki woh sach mein parallel hai.
problem.en: A line l is drawn on a page, and a point P is 6 cm above l. Using a ruler and a set-square, draw a line m through P parallel to l, and check that it really is parallel.

simpler.hi: Line l ke 6 cm upar ek bindu P hai. P se hokar l ke parallel line m kheenchni hai, aur jaanchna hai ki woh parallel hai.
simpler.en: A point P is 6 cm above line l. We draw a line m through P parallel to l, and check that it is parallel.

givens.en: there is a line l on the page

givens.hi: bindu P, l se 6 cm upar hai
givens.en: point P is 6 cm above l
a ruler and a set-square are available

find.hi: P se hokar l ke parallel line m, aur uski jaanch
find.en: a line m through P parallel to l, and a check

do.hi: Set-square ki ek bhuja line l par theek rakho
do.en: Place one edge of the set-square exactly on line l

steps.result: set-square ki bhuja l ke upar

why.hi: isi bhuja ki disha nayi line ko deni hai
why.en: this edge's direction is what the new line must have

simpler.hi: Pehle set-square ki ek bhuja ko line l ke bilkul upar rakho.
simpler.en: First lay one edge of the set-square right on line l.

do.hi: Ruler ko set-square ki doosri bhuja se sata kar kas kar pakdo
do.en: Hold the ruler firmly against another edge of the set-square

steps.result: ruler sthir, set-square ke liye raasta

why.hi: ruler ke saath khiskaane par set-square ghumta nahi
why.en: sliding along the ruler, the set-square does not turn

simpler.hi: Ab ruler ko set-square ki doosri bhuja se chipka kar rakho, aur use hilne mat do.
simpler.en: Now hold the ruler tight against another edge of the set-square, and do not let it move.

do.hi: Set-square ko ruler ke saath khiskao jab tak wahi bhuja P tak na pahunche, phir us bhuja ke saath line m kheencho
do.en: Slide the set-square along the ruler until that same edge reaches P, then draw line m along that edge

steps.result: line m, P se hokar, l ki disha mein

why.hi: khiskaane se bhuja ki disha nahi badli
why.en: sliding did not change the edge's direction

simpler.hi: Set-square ko ruler ke saath khiskao jab tak wahi bhuja P ko chhoo le. Wahan line kheencho, yahi line m hai.
simpler.en: Slide the set-square along the ruler until that same edge touches P. Draw a line there; that is line m.

prompt.hi: Ab jaanch karo: l aur m ke beech do door-door jagah doori naapi. Agar m sach mein parallel hai, toh dono jagah doori kitni aani chahiye?
prompt.en: Now check: the gap between l and m is measured at two places far apart. If m really is parallel, what should the gap be at both places?

simpler.hi: Parallel lines mein doori har jagah ek jaisi rehti hai. Socho, P line l se kitna upar tha.
simpler.en: Parallel lines keep the same gap everywhere. Think how far above line l the point P was.

why.hi: bindu P l ke upar 6 cm par hai, line m P se hokar parallel hai, toh doori 6 cm
why.en: point P is 6 cm above l, and m goes through P parallel to l, so the gap is 6 cm

answer.hi: line m, P se hokar l ke parallel hai, aur dono jagah doori 6 cm aati hai
answer.en: line m passes through P parallel to l, and the gap is 6 cm at both places

why.hi: khiskaane par set-square ki bhuja ki disha nahi badli, aur doori har jagah barabar hai toh l aur m kabhi nahi milengi
why.en: sliding did not change the direction of the set-square's edge, and with the gap equal everywhere, l and m will never meet

prompt.hi: {friend} ne set-square ko seedha rakh kar ek tirchhi crossing jaanchi, aur kona fit nahi hua. Phir set-square ghumaya toh kona theek fit ho gaya. Kya lines perpendicular hain, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: {friend} checked a tilted crossing with the set-square held straight, and the corner did not fit. Then {friend} turned the set-square and the corner fitted exactly. Are the lines perpendicular, yes or no?

why.hi: seedha set-square fit nahi hua, par ghumaya set-square theek fit hua, toh angle 90° hai
why.en: the straight set-square did not fit, but the turned set-square fitted exactly, so the angle is 90°

simpler.hi: Set-square ko ghuma kar jaanchna bilkul theek hai. Kona theek fit ho gaya, iska matlab angle kaisa hai, yeh socho.
simpler.en: Turning the set-square to check is perfectly fine. Think what it means for the angle that the corner fitted exactly.

prompt.hi: Set-square khiskaate waqt ruler hil gaya. Nayi line pichhli line se baayein 5 cm aur daayein 4.6 cm door hai. Yeh lines baayein taraf milengi, daayein taraf, ya kabhi nahi milengi?
prompt.en: The ruler moved while the set-square was being slid. The new line is 5 cm from the old one on the left and 4.6 cm on the right. Will these lines meet on the left, on the right, or never?

why.hi: doori baayein 5 cm se daayein 4.6 cm ho gayi, yaani daayi taraf ghat rahi hai, toh lines daayi taraf milengi
why.en: the gap shrinks from 5 cm on the left to 4.6 cm on the right, so they meet on the right

simpler.hi: Dekho doori kis taraf chhoti ho rahi hai. Jidhar doori ghatti hai, lines usi taraf milti hain.
simpler.en: See which way the gap is getting smaller. Lines meet on the side where the gap shrinks.

ladder.why: say how a set-square or folded paper corner checks a crossing for 90°
choose the set-square move that draws a perpendicular through a marked point
real shelves 30 cm and 31.5 cm apart: not parallel, and say what to fix

remediation.move: a right-angle tester (set-square or a twice-folded paper corner) is turned to match the crossing, never the crossing to match the page; the corner fits → perpendicular, whatever the tilt

say.hi: Samkon jaanchne wala kona, chahe set-square ka ho ya mode hue kaagaz ka, crossing ke hisaab se ghumate hain. Lines kitni bhi tirchhi hon, kona fit ho jaaye toh woh perpendicular hain.
say.en: A right-angle corner, whether a set-square's or a folded paper's, is turned to match the crossing. However tilted the lines are, if the corner fits, they are perpendicular.

simpler.hi: Samkon wala kona crossing ke hisaab se ghumao. Kona fit ho jaaye toh lines perpendicular hain, chahe kitni bhi tirchhi hon.
simpler.en: Turn the right-angle corner to match the crossing. If it fits, the lines are perpendicular, however tilted they are.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne tirchhi crossing par set-square 30° ghumaya, tab kona theek fit hua. Crossing par angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: {friend} turned the set-square 30° on a tilted crossing; then its corner fitted. How many degrees is the angle there?

why.hi: set-square 30° ghumaya, par uska kona nahi badla, samkon hi raha; theek fit hua toh crossing ka angle 90°
why.en: turning the set-square 30° did not change its right-angle corner; it fitted exactly, so the crossing's angle is 90°

simpler.hi: Socho, set-square ghumane se uske kone ka angle badalta hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: Think whether turning the set-square changes the angle of its corner.

remediation.move: measure the gap at two places far apart, never just look for a touch: equal gaps → parallel; any difference, however small → the lines close in and meet beyond the page

say.hi: Jaanch ke liye do door-door jagah doori naapo. Doori thodi si bhi alag ho, toh lines aage jaakar milengi, chahe page par na milein.
say.en: To check, measure the gap at two places far apart. If the gap differs even a little, the lines will meet further on, even if they don't meet on the page.

simpler.hi: Do door-door jagah doori naapo. Doori zara bhi alag ho, toh lines aage jaakar milengi.
simpler.en: Measure the gap at two places far apart. If it differs even a little, the lines will meet further on.

prompt.hi: Do lines ki doori baayein 7 cm aur daayein 6.8 cm hai. Parallel banane ke liye daayein doori kitni aur badhani hogi?
prompt.en: Two lines are 7 cm apart on the left and 6.8 cm on the right. By how much must the right gap grow to make them parallel?

why.hi: baayein doori 7 cm aur daayein doori 6.8 cm hai, toh 7 − 6.8 = 0.2 cm
why.en: the left gap is 7 cm and the right gap 6.8 cm, so 7 − 6.8 = 0.2 cm

simpler.hi: Parallel ke liye daayein doori bhi 7 cm honi chahiye. 7 cm mein se 6.8 cm ghatao.
simpler.en: For parallel, the right gap must also be 7 cm. Subtract 6.8 cm from 7 cm.
